title: Constructibility of all reductions from the first one

proof.text: Put $t=\pi_E$, $B=\cO_{E,X}$, $\Lambda_j=\cO_E/t^j$ and $R_j=(\Lambda_j)_X$. Every $\Lambda_j$ is a finite commutative ring: [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] supplies the nonarchimedean absolute value on $E$; [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] says its valuation ring is a DVR with finite residue field and that $t$ generates its maximal ideal; [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], clause (2), then applies to give finiteness for every $j\ge1$. The coefficient sheaf $(\Lambda_j)_X=p_X^*\underline{\Lambda_j}$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] is the constant sheaf of rings with value $\Lambda_j$: the condensed set of the finite discrete set $\Lambda_j$ is represented by the finite profinite set $\Lambda_j$, and $p_X^*$ is the inverse image along $u_X$ ([sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], clause 4), so it sends this representable to the sheaf represented by $X[\Lambda_j]=\coprod_{\Lambda_j}X$, which represents the constant sheaf by [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], clause 1; the ring structures agree since both are induced by the ring operations of $\Lambda_j$. For these finite rings, the constructibility conventions in [sk-def-sfb-constructible] and [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] agree: the coefficient sheaf is constant, a finitely presented module is a quotient of a finite free module and hence finite as a set; conversely a finite module admits a surjection from a finite free module, whose kernel is finite and hence finitely generated. A constant local model $\Lambda_U\otimes_\Lambda P$ is the constant sheaf of $P$: both are the sheafification of the constant module presheaf $P$. Thus both definitions ask for finite constant local models on a finite constructible stratification. Here $X$ is Noetherian, hence qcqs, so the global finite-stratification clause applies.

source.place: Second paragraph: finite torsion coefficients and the classical finite-stalk constructibility convention.

proof.text:
For $n>1$ the first assertion of [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution] identifies $R_j=B/t^jB$ and says multiplication by $t$ on $B$ is injective. Consequently
$$0\longrightarrow R_{n-1}\xrightarrow{\ t\ }R_n\longrightarrow R_1\longrightarrow0$$
is a short exact sequence of $R_n$-modules, with scalar structures through $R_n\to R_{n-1}$ and $R_n\to R_1$. Indeed the first map sends the local class of $b$ to the class of $tb$; if $tb=t^nc$, injectivity of multiplication by $t$ gives $b=t^{n-1}c$, so the map is injective. The kernel of the final quotient is precisely the local classes divisible by $t$, which is the image of the first map. Quotient sheaf sections have such representatives locally; this proves sheaf exactness. All maps are $R_n$-linear by the displayed formulas. Kernels and sheafified cokernels compute exactness in module sheaves by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so this is exact in that coefficient category as well.

source.place: Second paragraph: the coefficient short exact sequence, with its R_n-linear structure made explicit.

proof.text:
Choose a representing complex for $K$. By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] it has a K-flat resolution $P^\bullet$ with flat $B$-module terms; there is no boundedness assumption on $K$. By the exact-functor definition [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], tensoring the preceding sequence with each $P^a$ preserves its kernel and cokernel, yielding a degreewise short exact sequence
$$0\to P^\bullet\otimes_B R_{n-1}\to P^\bullet\otimes_B R_n\to P^\bullet\otimes_B R_1\to0.$$
These are complexes of $R_n$-modules with the action on the second tensor factor, and their differentials and the sequence maps are $R_n$-linear. Exactness of the underlying module sheaves is exactness here, by the kernel/cokernel description in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] in the abelian category of $R_n$-module sheaves. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] each $P^\bullet\otimes_B R_j$ represents $K_j$ in its own coefficient category; regarding the same complex as an $R_n$-complex therefore gives a distinguished triangle
$$\operatorname{Res}_{R_n\to R_{n-1}}K_{n-1}\longrightarrow K_n\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_{R_n\to R_1}K_1\longrightarrow(\operatorname{Res}_{R_n\to R_{n-1}}K_{n-1})[1]$$
in $D(R_n)$. In particular this constructs the required triangle with the quotient-ring action, rather than inferring that action from a triangle only in $D(B)$.

source.place: Second paragraph: applying derived tensor to the coefficient sequence; the construction uses Stacks 06YS, 03ER, 06YY and 0152.

proof.text: For $1\le j\le n$, restriction along $R_n\to R_j$ preserves bounded constructibility. Indeed [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] leaves the underlying abelian sheaf unchanged. Kernels and sheafified cokernels are unchanged by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so this restriction is exact and the cohomology of a restricted complex is the restricted cohomology. In the definition [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], keep the same finite stratification and the same pro-étale covers trivializing a constructible $R_j$-sheaf. A constant local model $M$ becomes the same constant sheaf with $\Lambda_n$ acting through $\Lambda_n\to\Lambda_j$; this follows directly by applying that scalar action to local constant sections and their gluings, and commutes with restriction to each stratum. Its stalk set is unchanged and finite. Thus it is a finite $\Lambda_n$-module and these same models witness constructibility. Cohomological vanishing bounds are unchanged as well.

source.place: Second paragraph, last sentence: restriction of scalars preserves constructibility; the finite local models are unchanged.

proof.text: Assume (1), and fix integers $r\le s$ such that $H^q(K_1)=0$ outside $[r,s]$. Induct on $n\ge1$, asserting both bounded constructibility and this same bound for $K_n$. The base case is the hypothesis. For $n>1$, the preceding scalar-restriction argument puts the two outer terms of the preceding triangle in $\Dbc(X,\Lambda_n)$. By step 2, $\Lambda_n$ is finite commutative. The scheme $X$ and this ring satisfy all hypotheses of [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated], whose distinguished-triangle clause therefore gives bounded constructibility of the middle term $K_n$ over $\Lambda_n$.

source.place: Second paragraph: induction and closure of bounded constructible finite-coefficient complexes under distinguished triangles; Stacks 09B5, 09AL and 06UQ.

proof.text:
For the same inductive step, [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] applied in $D(R_n)$ gives the exact segment
$$H^q(K_{n-1})\longrightarrow H^q(K_n)\longrightarrow H^q(K_1).$$
The outer sheaves here have the restricted $R_n$-actions described above. For $q<r$ or $q>s$, both are zero, by the induction hypothesis and the chosen bound for $K_1$. Exactness forces $H^q(K_n)=0$. This completes the induction with the identical interval $[r,s]$ for all $n$, proving $(1)\Rightarrow(2)$.

source.place: Second paragraph: the long exact sequence gives the uniform interval; Stacks 05RS and 0147.

proof.text: For the final interpretation, [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], clause 3, identifies the pulled-back coefficient sheaf $B$ with the completed coefficient sheaf $\varprojlim_j R_j$ as sheaves of rings, and [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients] fixes the same finite-reduction tower and canonical completion map. In particular the K-flat representative $P^\bullet$ used above computes exactly the reductions of [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] over this completed sheaf. By [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], the canonical map $\varphi:K\to L=R\varprojlim_n K_n$ is an isomorphism. Write its Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-limit] as $L\xrightarrow{\iota}\prod_n\operatorname{Res} K_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_n\operatorname{Res} K_n\xrightarrow{\delta_L}L[1]$. The canonical map has $\iota\varphi=(c_n)_n$, with $c_n:K\to\operatorname{Res}K_n$ the reduction maps. Hence $( (c_n)_n,1-s,\varphi[1]^{-1}\delta_L)$ is a distinguished triangle, being isomorphic to this Roos triangle through $(\varphi,\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})$. This is precisely the completeness condition of [def-weil-derived-complete]. Finally [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] require the identical finite locally closed constructible stratifications, locally constant restrictions and finite module stalks. By [def-weil-cohomological-support], $\operatorname{Supp}_{\mathrm{coh}}(K_n)\subseteq[r,s]$ says exactly that $\mathcal H^q(K_n)=0$ for $q\notin[r,s]$. Thus, under the already assumed completeness, the remaining conditions of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] are exactly (2), and the equivalence proved above replaces them by (1). The definition [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] is stated for $\ell\neq p$, with $p$ the prime of the fixed global finite-field datum, and this interpretation is made in that range; the equivalence $(1)\Leftrightarrow(2)$ proved in steps 1-7 uses no such hypothesis, and neither the completed sheaf nor the displayed predicates depends on $p$. No Tor-amplitude condition is inserted.
